content.text:
This is one axial slice of a T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI (radiological convention: patient right on image left, anterior at top). It contains a fibrous soft-tissue tumor.

The left panel is the clean image; the right panel shows numbered marks. Choose the ONE mark that lies inside the tumor, as close to its centre as possible. End your reply with a final line exactly: ANSWER: <mark number>

This axial slice appears to be of the abdomen or pelvis. The large bright heterogeneous mass in the anterior abdomen, with the kidney-like structure at the posterior, looks like the tumor, although the bowel loops are also bright.

The circled (yellow) marks are 886, 842, 890, 933 and 862. Mark 933 sits on a very bright round structure, which is probably a vessel or the bladder. Mark 862 is in the posterior kidney-like structure. The anterior bright mass, which spans roughly x 310-500 and y 110-350, is the likely tumor. Marks 886, 842 and 890 all lie within it.

Its centre is about x 390, y 230. Mark 890 at (1157, 327) corresponds to x 372 in the left panel after subtracting the 785 px panel offset, at y 327. Mark 842 at (1219, 282) corresponds to x 434, y 282. Mark 886 at (1137, 123) corresponds to x 352, y 123.

Mark 890 is closest to the centre of the mass, although it sits near the lower edge on a darker line. Mark 842 is at the right side, within a bright area. Mark 886 is at the top, within a bright area.

I'll pick 890, the closest to the centre of the mass, although this is uncertain.

ANSWER: 890
